claim: The merge event fires nothing: both driver Routines are pure hourly crons, so a chain edge that relies on a merge to fire the next cycle silently waits for the next cron slot.
No session can fire a UI-created Routine: the platform refuses with 'Agents can only fire routines they created', so a fire_trigger chain edge is dead on arrival for every session.
A chain one-shot must create a FRESH session and INHERIT its creator's environment; an environment-less one-shot strands the session it fires (the cycle-02 recovery-by-git-bundle).
A purchase self-merge must never chain into another purchase: one price list may only be bought from once, so the edge fires the CORPUS driver.
An intake-selection rule that depends on being 'the cycle immediately after a purchase' cannot live in session memory: cycle 23 was that cycle and consumed --ready anyway, stranding paid supply.
The unblock route may only name signals met by LANDED purchases with live refused groups; an open row's signal would promise supply nobody has paid for.
A ceremony fence keyed on the PR TITLE fires on the author's self-declaration: a purchase-shaped diff under another title skips it entirely.
A detailed PR body over an empty diff is a report-without-push; nothing but a human reading get_files detected it until the non-empty-diff fence existed.
CGB_LEAN must force the suite gate OFF as well as on: in a lean-local container 113 gated tests become real full-Mathlib elaborations and the per-commit gate goes from ~90s to hours.
The rule-3 capability classification must not consult the suite gate, or CGB_LEAN=0 makes a capable container read as yield-worthy.
The download-host list for the Lean closure is measured-so-far, never proven-total: read the sources that name the hosts, never recall them.
prose_only_reason: names an external service's behaviour, which no test in this repo can execute; the closure's own failure output is the only measurement, and it changes when the vendor changes

claim: git push --delete through the proxy can 403 and still exit 0 with 'Everything up-to-date' while the ref survives: verify with ls-remote, never with the exit code.
prose_only_reason: an observed behaviour of the git proxy in this environment; reproducing it in a test would require a proxy that lies on demand, and the repo-side auto-delete setting has since removed the need

claim: A lexical census cannot tell a theorem from a proof remark: a stand-in reading of a proof remark passes every gate with ok=True.
prose_only_reason: the refusal is a HONESTY-rule judgment about what a subject IS, not a predicate over the reading; mechanizing it would require deciding theoremhood from prose, which is the open problem the whole operation is about

claim: Two measurements that disagree (a local elaboration that succeeds vs one that fails on the same tree) are recorded as a disagreement, never silently resolved in the current session's favour.
prose_only_reason: a rule about how a session REPORTS conflicting evidence; the conflict itself is environment-dependent and no committed test can stage two contradictory containers

claim: A loop guard that branches on machine-readable state must be a tool the prompt runs, never a paragraph the prompt recites: a paragraph cannot be tested at its thresholds.
The pre-claim freshness guard and the post-claim tie-break are separate questions: reusing the pre-claim verdict after claiming makes a session exit on its own draft and leave the lock as litter.
A recorded lesson must cite a tooth that resolves or declare why it has no executable form; free-text lessons are how mechanization debt accumulates one sentence at a time.

CLAUDE.md's own invariants can go stale: 'no local Lean in remote containers' survived a day past the egress change that falsified it, because the router is prose about the world rather than a derivation from it.
prose_only_reason: an invariant about the ENVIRONMENT, not about the tree; no committed test can observe the network policy or the image contents, which is why tools/lean_env_probe.py must be RUN in-session rather than read off disk
